en: The Therāpadāna, Timira Chapter 3: The Apadāna of the Elder Nippannajalika I was once a king named Sivi, ruling over the kingdom of Aṅga. At that time, the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Perfectly Enlightened One, the one endowed with knowledge and conduct, the Sugata, the Knower of the worlds, the unsurpassed guide who tames those to be tamed, the Teacher of gods and humans, the Buddha, the Bhagavān, was dwelling at the city of Aṅgāvatī. Having heard of his fame, I went to him and paid homage. Then, having offered a pair of garments, I sat down to one side. Seated there, I addressed the Blessed One with these verses: “O Sage, you who are free from all stains, Who have transcended all states of existence, Who have reached the further shore of the ocean of suffering— To you, the peerless one, I pay homage. Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Perfectly Enlightened One, knowing my intention, taught me the Dhamma in its various aspects. Having heard the Dhamma, I attained the fruit of stream-entry. Then, rising from my seat and circumambulating the Blessed One three times, I departed. As I was walking along the road, a thorn pierced my foot. While I was lying down in pain, I extended my joined palms toward the Blessed One and made this aspiration: “By this root of merit, may I become a Buddha in the future, One who has crossed over the flood, liberated from all bonds, And who, having reached the further shore of the ocean of suffering, May I lead others across as well. Through that wholesome deed, I passed through many births, And in each successive life, I was born into a noble family. In my final birth, I was born into the lineage of the Sakyas, And I became a son of the King of the Śākyas. Having gone forth from the household life into homelessness, I have realized the state of an Arhat. My mind is liberated, and I am free from all defilements; I have attained the goal for which I went forth. Thus, by the power of that former aspiration, I have now become an Arhat. This is the account of the Elder Nippannajalika, Told in detail according to the truth.
“Sitting at the foot of a tree,
afflicted by a supreme malady,
I have reached a state of extreme compassion.”
In a forest grove,
out of compassion,
the Teacher approached me.
Thus, lying down,
with my head bowed and palms joined in reverence,
I was clear-minded and joyful in heart.
Having paid homage to the Fully Enlightened One, the supreme among all beings,
I passed away there.
In the ninety-two aeons since I paid homage to that Supreme Person,
I have not known a state of misery.
This is the fruit of that salutation.
In the fifth aeon from now,
there were five named Mahāsikha.
Possessing the seven treasures,
they are wheel-turning monarchs of great power.
The four analytical knowledges—
the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.
Thus indeed did the Venerable Nippannajalika Thera speak these verses.
The legend of the Elder Nipannajalikaṭṭha is the third.
